name: What is the best project timeline for a multi-family renovation?

mainEntity.name: How long does a typical multi-family renovation take from planning to closeout?
mainEntity.text: How long does a typical multi-family renovation take from planning to closeout?

acceptedAnswer.text: There is no single timeline for a multi-family renovation because the schedule depends on scope, permit requirements, occupancy, and how many units or building systems are involved. A smaller interior refresh can move relatively quickly, while a full property repositioning with phased work may take many months. Planning time matters as much as construction time because design development, budgeting, permit review, and procurement can add significant lead time before work even begins. In occupied buildings, phasing and resident coordination also lengthen the schedule. The best way to estimate the timeline is to break it into preconstruction, permitting, procurement, field work, inspections, punch list, and closeout. Each phase should have its own milestones and buffer time for delays. In Los Angeles and surrounding areas, inspection timing and logistics often affect the finish date. A realistic schedule is usually more valuable than an aggressive one that keeps slipping.
acceptedAnswer.description: The timeline depends on unit count, occupancy, scope, permits, and material lead times. Small renovations may take a few months, while larger phased projects can take many months or longer because design, approvals, procurement, construction, and inspections all add time.
